title: Stamping the Grid
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix with empty and occupied cells, determine if it's possible to place stamps of a specified size without covering any occupied cells and ensuring all empty cells are covered, allowing overlaps and without rotating the stamps.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix with empty and occupied cells, determine if it's possible to place stamps of a specified size without covering any occupied cells and ensuring all empty cells are covered, allowing overlaps and without rotating the stamps.
constraints: grid is a nonempty binary matrix; stamps cannot rotate or cover occupied cells.
Stamps may overlap and must stay within the grid.
Return whether every zero cell can be covered by at least one valid stamp.
hints: Use a rectangle-sum table to identify valid empty placements, then a 2D difference array to combine their coverage.
For every top-left position, query whether its stamp rectangle sum is zero and range-add that rectangle.
Prefix the difference grid; reject any original zero whose resulting coverage is zero.
Every added rectangle is legal, overlaps are allowed, and the final coverage test is exactly the requirement for each empty cell.
editorial: Every added rectangle is legal, overlaps are allowed, and the final coverage test is exactly the requirement for each empty cell.

tests.explanation: Two overlapping 4-by-3 stamps cover every zero without touching the occupied first column.
Every 4-by-4 placement touches an occupied cell, so the zeros cannot all be covered.
